question: What is the recommended way to prevent trailers from rolling over when pulling doubles or triples?
choice_a: Steer gently and go slowly around corners, ramps, and curves
choice_b: Accelerate through curves to maintain momentum
choice_c: Brake hard mid-curve to reduce speed quickly
choice_d: Keep the same speed used for a single trailer combination
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to steer gently and go slowly around corners, ramps, off ramps, and curves, noting that a safe speed for a single trailer may be too fast for doubles or triples.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7.1.1, Page 83

question: In a set of doubles or triples, which trailer is most likely to turn over because of the crack-the-whip effect?
choice_a: The first trailer directly behind the tractor
choice_b: The last trailer in the combination
choice_d: All trailers turn over with equal likelihood
explanation: The manual explains that doubles and triples are more likely to turn over because of the crack-the-whip effect, and the last trailer in a combination is most likely to turn over.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7.1.2, Page 83

question: Why do doubles and triples require more following distance and space management than other commercial vehicles?
choice_a: They are longer and cannot be turned or stopped suddenly, so more following distance and larger gaps are needed
choice_b: They have better braking performance and can follow more closely
choice_c: State law caps their speed at 25 mph regardless of road type
choice_d: They are exempt from following distance rules
explanation: The manual explains that doubles and triples take up more space, are longer, and cannot be turned or stopped suddenly, so drivers must allow more following distance and larger gaps before entering or crossing traffic.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7.1.5, Page 83

question: Why must drivers be especially careful with doubles and triples in bad weather or mountain driving?
choice_a: They have greater length and more dead axles to pull with the drive axles, increasing chances of skids and loss of traction
choice_b: Doubles and triples are not permitted on mountain roads under any conditions
choice_c: Their brakes are disabled automatically in wet weather
choice_d: They have fewer axles than single-trailer rigs, reducing traction
explanation: The manual notes that in adverse conditions, drivers of doubles and triples have greater length and more dead axles to pull with their drive axles than other drivers, creating more chance for skids and loss of traction.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7.1.6, Page 83

question: How can you identify a converter dolly equipped with anti-lock brakes, as required for dollies built on or after March 1, 1998?
choice_a: It has a yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly
choice_b: It has a red lamp on the rear bumper
choice_c: It has a green lamp on the fifth wheel
choice_d: There is no visible indicator; you must check the manufacturer's plate
explanation: The manual states converter dollies built on or after March 1, 1998 are required to have anti-lock brakes, and these dollies will have a yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7.1.8, Page 83

question: What is a converter dolly, as defined in the Colorado CDL Manual?
choice_a: A coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semi-trailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig
choice_b: A hand tool used to tighten the kingpin locking jaws
choice_c: A hydraulic ramp used to load trailers onto rail cars
choice_d: A device that automatically balances trailer weight distribution
explanation: The manual defines a converter dolly as a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel that couples a semi-trailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7.2, Page 84

question: When coupling twin trailers, if the second (rear) trailer does not have spring brakes, how do you set its emergency brakes before backing the dolly under it?
choice_a: Connect the emergency line, charge the trailer air tank, then disconnect the emergency line to set the brakes
choice_b: Apply the tractor's parking brake only
choice_c: Deflate the trailer tires to prevent rolling
choice_d: Leave the trailer unsecured since it has no brakes to set
explanation: The manual explains that if the second trailer lacks spring brakes, the driver should connect the emergency line, charge the trailer air tank, and disconnect the emergency line, which sets the trailer emergency brakes if the slack adjusters are correctly adjusted; chock the wheels if in doubt.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7.2.1, Page 84

question: For the safest handling on the road when pulling doubles, where should the more heavily loaded semi-trailer be positioned?
choice_a: In the first position directly behind the tractor
choice_b: In the rear position, behind the lighter trailer
choice_c: Loading order does not affect handling
choice_d: Split evenly between both trailers regardless of position
explanation: The manual states that for the safest handling on the road, the more heavily loaded semi-trailer should be in the first position behind the tractor, with the lighter trailer in the rear.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7.2.1, Page 84

question: After coupling the converter dolly to the second (rear) trailer, how should you test the coupling?
choice_a: By pulling against the pin of the second semi-trailer
choice_b: By driving forward at highway speed
choice_c: By releasing all air from the system
choice_d: By checking only the electrical cord connection
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to test the coupling by pulling against the pin of the second semi-trailer before making the visual check of the coupling.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7.2.1, Page 85

question: Why should you never unlock the pintle hook while the converter dolly is still under the rear trailer?
choice_a: The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making it very difficult to re-couple
choice_b: It will cause the trailer's electrical system to short out
choice_c: It automatically triggers the trailer's emergency brakes to release
choice_d: It has no safety consequence, only a minor inconvenience
explanation: The manual explicitly warns to never unlock the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer, because the dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making it very difficult to re-couple.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7.2.2, Page 85

question: What is the correct order for uncoupling a triple-trailer rig?
choice_a: Uncouple the third trailer first by pulling the dolly out and unhitching it, then uncouple the remainder of the rig as a double-bottom rig
choice_b: Uncouple the tractor first, leaving all three trailers connected
choice_d: Uncouple the first trailer first, then work toward the rear
explanation: The manual describes uncoupling a triple-trailer rig by first uncoupling the third trailer, pulling the dolly out, and unhitching it using the doubles method, then uncoupling the remainder of the rig as a double-bottom rig.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7.2.3, Page 85

question: When inspecting the upper fifth wheel on a doubles/triples combination, where should the locking jaws be closed?
choice_a: Around the shank of the kingpin, not the head
choice_b: Around the head of the kingpin, not the shank
choice_c: Anywhere on the kingpin, position does not matter
choice_d: On the glide plate, not the kingpin
explanation: The manual's inspection checklist specifies checking that locking jaws are around the shank, not the head, of the kingpin.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7.3.1, Page 85

question: On a set of double or triple trailers, what should the shut-off valve position be at the rear of the front trailer(s) compared to the rear of the last trailer?
choice_a: Rear of front trailer(s) OPEN; rear of the last trailer CLOSED
choice_b: Rear of front trailer(s) CLOSED; rear of the last trailer OPEN
choice_c: Both should be CLOSED at all times
choice_d: Both should be OPEN at all times
explanation: The manual's inspection list states shut-off valves at the rear of front trailers should be OPEN, while the rear of the last trailer should be CLOSED, along with a CLOSED converter dolly air tank drain valve.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7.3.1, Page 86

topic: Checking Air Flow to All Trailers
question: How do you check that air flows all the way to the last trailer in a set of doubles or triples?
choice_a: Push in the red trailer air supply knob, go to the rear of the rig, and open the emergency line shut-off valve at the last trailer to listen for escaping air
choice_b: Watch the fuel gauge for a sudden pressure drop
choice_c: Rev the engine and listen for a hiss from the cab
choice_d: Check only that the headlights on the last trailer illuminate
explanation: The manual explains that after pushing in the trailer air supply knob to charge the emergency lines, the driver should go to the rear of the rig and open the emergency line shut-off valve at the last trailer; hearing air escaping shows the entire system is charged.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7.4.1, Page 86

question: During the tractor protection valve test on a doubles/triples rig, at approximately what pressure range should the trailer air supply control pop out to the emergency position?
choice_a: Usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi
choice_b: Usually within the range of 60 to 90 psi
choice_d: Only when the tanks are completely drained to 0 psi
explanation: The manual states the trailer air supply control (tractor protection valve control) should pop out, or go from normal to emergency position, when air pressure falls into the manufacturer-specified range, usually 20 to 45 psi.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7.4.1, Page 86

question: When testing trailer service brakes on a doubles/triples rig using the hand control (trolley valve), what confirms the brakes are connected and working?
choice_a: You should feel the brakes come on
choice_b: The trailer air supply knob pops out automatically
choice_c: The parking brakes release on their own
choice_d: The dolly landing gear lowers automatically
explanation: The manual explains that applying trailer brakes with the hand valve while moving forward slowly should produce a felt braking effect, confirming the trailer brakes are connected and working, though normal operation uses the foot pedal.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7.4.1, Page 87
